rows.english: Cannot create the undo cache. Free some device storage and try again.
rows.value: ⵓⵔ ⵉⵣⵎⵉⵔ AN Paint ⴰⴷ ⵉⵙⵏⵓⵍⴼⵓ ⴰⴷⵖⴰⵔ ⵏ ⵉⴼⵓⵢⵍⴰ ⵏ «ⵙⵙⵔ». ⵙⵙⴰⴳⴰ ⴽⵔⴰ ⵏ ⵓⴷⵖⴰⵔ ⵉ ⵓⵃⴹⴰⵡ ⵏ ⵉⴼⵓⵢⵍⴰ, ⴰⵔⵎ ⴷⵉⵖ.
rows.backtranslation: AN Paint cannot create the location for Undo files. Make some space available for saving files, then try again.
rows.context_and_review_note: Normalized again to diɣ, consistent with the reviewed Try again messages. Retained Undo-file location as the functional disk-cache directory and space for saving files as storage, not RAM. RasterHistory.kt:22 and :51 issue this error when the session directory cannot be created; the message does not assert disk-full is the only possible cause, that files were erased, or that freeing space guarantees success. The storage remedy is comprehensible in this local app operation without inventing a new device noun, though device-local is implicit rather than explicitly named. The quoted Undo label matches ui_undo. No advice to close apps instead of freeing storage is substituted.

rows.english: The canvas was restored, but its undo history could not be read. The original draft has been kept as a recovery copy.
rows.value: ⵉⵙⵙⵓⴽⵏ AN Paint ⴰⴷⵖⴰⵔ ⵏ ⵓⵙⵙⵓⵏⵖ, ⵎⴰⵛⴰ ⵓⵔ ⵉⵣⵎⵉⵔ ⴰⴷ ⵉⵖⵔ ⵉⵙⴼⴽⴰ ⵏ «ⵙⵙⵔ». ⵉⵜⵜⵓⵙⵙⵏⵖⵍ ⵓⴼⴰⵢⵍⵓ ⴰⵏⴰⵚⵍⵉ ⵉⵜⵜⵡⴰⵃⴹⴰⵏ ⵙ ⵓⵡⵔⵎⴰⵏ ⵖⵔ ⵢⴰⵏ ⵓⴼⴰⵢⵍⵓ ⵢⴰⴹⵏ ⵃⵎⴰ ⴰⴷ ⵜⵙⵙⵓⴽⵏⴷ ⵜⴰⵡⵍⴰⴼⵜ.
rows.backtranslation: AN Paint restored the canvas, but cannot read the Undo data. The original automatically saved file has been copied to another file for recovering the image.
rows.context_and_review_note: Retained restored drawing area, unreadable Undo data, and a separate copy of the original autosaved file for image recovery. The passive copy wording describes an actual file copy, not restored history or recovery of unsaved-newer edits. EditorDraftRecovery.kt calls document.replace(draft.image), then in historyFailed calls preserveForRecovery(retainOriginal=true) BEFORE assigning this notice. AutosaveStore.kt:67–89 keeps read/recovery/preserve in the same I/O-lock transaction; :100–113 copies the source into an AtomicFile, explicitly fd.syncs, and calls finishWrite before returning. Exceptions call failWrite and propagate; recovery catches exceptions/OOM and replaces this notice with the preservation/retry or paused-autosave failure path. Thus the application-level claim is gated on copy completion. This is a static call-order/failure-path assessment, not filesystem fault-injection proof or an indefinite-retention guarantee. Recovery-purpose wording does not promise readable Undo history.
